title: Imperial Sugar: combustible-dust accumulation, enclosure change, and normalization of deviance
summary: Imperial Sugar is encoded as a combustible-dust process-safety record: dust accumulation, enclosure modification without hazard evaluation, absent dust removal/venting, and normalization of deviance created a major-accident pathway.

status_history.note: Added as process-safety / CSB lane record.

subjects.name: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board

claims.claim: The CSB investigation page records the Imperial Sugar event as a February 7, 2008 combustible-dust explosion and fire at Port Wentworth, Georgia; it caused 14 deaths and 38 injuries, and the explosion was fueled by massive accumulations of combustible sugar dust throughout the packaging building.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The CSB final report says Imperial Sugar enclosed granulated-sugar belt conveyors in 2007 but did not evaluate the hazards associated with generating and accumulating combustible dust inside the new enclosure, did not install dust removal to keep dust below the MEC, and did not equip enclosures with deflagration vents.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The CSB final report explicitly applies normalization of deviance: known combustible-sugar-dust hazards and unsafe work practices persisted because years of operation without a major catastrophe relaxed the effective performance standard.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: For the cube, Imperial Sugar is a combustible-dust barrier-health record: a sanitation/quality change and recurring accumulation problem became a major-hazard control failure, not a mere housekeeping footnote.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The Imperial Sugar record also calibrates warning-governance and correction-memory patterns because known hazards, prior incidents/audits, and industry knowledge did not convert into effective dust-control design, maintenance, or housekeeping before catastrophe.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.system: sugar refinery packaging building, conveyor enclosures, dust-control and housekeeping system

sequence_of_events.event: Combustible sugar dust accumulated in facility areas.
Conveyor enclosure change concentrated dust without corresponding hazard evaluation, dust removal, or venting.
Ignition and propagation through accumulated dust caused catastrophic explosions and fire.
CSB interpreted persistence of known conditions as normalization of deviance.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Combustible sugar dust explosion propagated through dust accumulations and vulnerable enclosed spaces.
contributing_factors: unrecognized/unevaluated hazard introduced by enclosure modification
known hazards not translated into corrective action
latent_conditions: long operation without catastrophe normalized rejectable dust conditions
combustible-dust hazards treated too much like cleanliness/quality issues and too little like major accident hazards

handling_notes: Preserve worker/community dignity and avoid casualty spectacle.
